# aperv-tool test fixtures

Two fixture classes serve the analysis layer, and confusing them is the mistake the
separation exists to prevent.

**FIXTURE-REAL** is recorded campaign output — cmp162 below, and the baseline sample.
It validates everything that touches a real file format: parsing, loading, factor
decomposition, admissibility, outcome building. What it cannot validate is whether an
estimator is *right*, because nobody knows cmp162's true effect. A negative-binomial IRR
checked against data whose IRR is unknown has not been checked.

**FIXTURE-SYNTH** is generated frames with closed-form or known answers, including the
degenerate shapes — all-zero paired differences, a saturated binary outcome, zero
discordant pairs, GLM separation. It is where estimator correctness is established.

Tests that reproduce a campaign artefact are therefore labelled **parity** tests
(INV-CAN-21): they prove the pipeline is unchanged, never that the number is right.

| File | Provenance |
|---|---|
| `trace_ndjson_golden.ndjson` | Hand-written from the wire-format authority: the `event-sink` spec of `ape`'s `rearch-04-step-ndjson-telemetry` (`StepRecord` schema, dictionary encoding, omitted-default rules), field by field. It is **not** a captured run — no stage-4 jar exists yet — and it is written first on purpose: a fixture derived from the reader would only test the reader against itself. It carries the adversarial cases a real run produces rarely or never, so they are exercised every build: a raw newline inside an action string (INV-SNK-02), a line of free `[APE] ` text that must be skipped without counting as malformed (INV-SNK-11: a sink record is a line beginning with `{`), one syntactically invalid record, and a final line truncated mid-write as a `SIGKILL` leaves it (the file deliberately ends without a newline). Contents: `RUN_START` with `t0=1750000000000`; `ACT` 17 (`mop:1`) and 18 (`mop:0`); `STATE` 231→act 17 and 232→act 18; step 42 with no boost fields, `patched:0`, two `llm[]` entries in occurrence order and an `out` resolving to a new state in activity 18 (so the step-side MOP flag is true and the outcome-side false); step 43 with boosts, `cf`, and no `patched` member, closed without an `out`; step 44 flushed with `out:{"resolved":false}`; plus `MOP_DATA` and `RUN_END`, which are well-formed records the reader ignores rather than counts. Expected: 3 step rows, `diagnostics.malformed == 2`. When a real stage-4 trace exists it is added *beside* this file, not in place of it. |
| `cmp162_manifest.json` | The pin of FIXTURE-REAL — see §cmp162 below. Regenerated by `build_cmp162_manifest.py`, never edited by hand. |
| `cryptoapp.apk.json` | Copy of `ape-rearch/src/test/resources/cryptoapp.apk.gh60-fresh.json`, the gh60 producer output for `br.unb.cic.cryptoapp` that the jar's own `MopDataTest` parses. Named as the pipeline names it (`<apk_name>.json`) so the derivation reads it exactly as it reads production output. It is the ground truth of `test_derive_cryptoapp_ground_truth`: 5 windows, 3 flagged widgets — one of them the Execute button recovered through the D8 synthetic-lambda rule — 4 activities and 1 provider. |

## cmp162 — FIXTURE-REAL

**The tree is a fixture, not a corpus.** No number computed on cmp162 answers a research
question; it exercises code paths against files a real campaign wrote. Recording that
structurally rather than only in prose is the point of `cmp162_manifest.json`: every file a
test reads is pinned by path *and* sha256, so a later refactor cannot quietly change what
"the tests pass" means.

**The tree lives outside this repository** — `experimento-comp162/`, roughly 40 GB of
campaign output, untracked. Nothing is copied in. When the tree is absent,
`test_fixture_manifest.py` skips the dependent tests with the reason `FIXTURE-REAL not
present`; a missing fixture is never a silent pass.

**Shape**, verified against the data rather than against the campaign plan: 162 applications
× 3 arms (`ape`, `aperv:mop_off_llm_off`, `aperv:mop_on_llm_off`) × 3 replicas × one timeout
(300 s) = 1458 identities, 1455 of them completed. 1458 `.trace` and 1458 `.logcat` files;
972 `.trace.ndjson.gz`, which are byte-identical gzips of their sibling `.trace` and must
never be counted as a second stream; 162 `<apk>.json`.

**Why the failures matter more than the successes.** All five consolidated CSVs hold
`COMPLETED` rows only — `performance.csv` has 1455 of 1455 — so a loader built on them sees a
campaign in which nothing went wrong. Every failure fact is visible only in `tasks.json`,
which is why the manifest measures its arithmetic there and records it as a fact:

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| task records | 1486 |
| identities | 1458 |
| identities with ≥1 `COMPLETED` | 1455 |
| dead identities | 3 — `com.ds.avare_404.apk` × `aperv:mop_on_llm_off`, replicas 1–3 |
| `ERROR` records, total | 31 |
| `ERROR` records on the dead identities | 9 (three each) |
| `ERROR` records on identities that later completed | 22, across 21 identities |

The two `ERROR` classes are worth keeping apart: 19 are `Failed to install app` — ~60 s,
coverage `0.0/0.0`, the application never ran — and 12 are `ToolExecutionComponent execution
failed` after 2–5 minutes, some of them carrying **non-zero coverage**. That second kind is why
the collision policy keeps the `COMPLETED` record with the larger coverage rather than the last
one: both records of such an identity hold a plausible number.

The tests assert against these manifest values, never against a literal.

**The pinned set.** All eight `tasks.json` and their five consolidated CSVs; the campaign's
own `consolidado/*.csv` and `censo_substrato.csv`; the 162 `<apk>.json`; the raw
`.trace`/`.logcat` pairs of a declared twelve-application subset; and the sixty
`aperv:mop_on_llm_off` traces the measured activity-visit distributions were computed over,
in sorted path order. `*.mop.json` is deliberately excluded — no reader under `analysis/`
may open one (INV-CAN-24), and pinning a file the library must never read would invite
exactly that.

**The twelve-application subset** is declared, not sampled. It holds the campaign's two
smoke applications (the runs whose `RUN_START` gates were checked by hand before the
campaign was allowed to proceed), `com.ds.avare_404.apk` for its real dead identities, a
single-activity and a multi-activity application for the segmenter, and seven more from the
first batch chosen so the subset overlaps the measured-figure basis.

**Regenerating**, from the rv-android root:

```bash
.venv/bin/python modules/aperv-tool/tests/fixtures/build_cmp162_manifest.py
```

Read-only over the campaign tree; no device, no emulator, no `adb` (INV-APV-35). It takes a
few minutes — the raw streams run to hundreds of megabytes and are hashed in full.

## `baseline_sample/` — FIXTURE-REAL for the baseline parsers

`ape` and `droidbot` emit no NDJSON, so the golden trace fixture says nothing about them,
and cmp162 has no `droidbot` arm at all. Their only source of real input is the E2 raw
corpus at `/home/pedro/desenvolvimento/RV_ANDROID_NOVO_DATASET/RESULTS` — 21,681 runs,
39.8 GB, outside any repository and read-only. A suite that required that tree would be
unrunnable anywhere else, so **twelve runs are copied in and pinned** by sha256 beside the
path each came from, in `baseline_sample_manifest.json`.

The twelve are chosen for the cases the parsers must get right, not sampled:

| arm | runs | what each is there for |
|---|---|---|
| `ape` | 6 | one trace with **no `SATA begin step` marker at all** — "no steps" is a first-class outcome, and a parser that raises there silently deletes a run from the denominator; one carrying a `// NOT RESPONDING` block, hoisted to a run-level event on the preceding step index rather than parsed as a step; one 300 s run that produced five steps; three ordinary 60 s runs |
| `droidbot` | 6 | all four policies (`bfs_greedy`, `bfs_naive`, `dfs_greedy`, `dfs_naive`); two runs at 300 s, and among them the rare one that reached an **orderly stop** (`Finish sending events` → `INFO:DroidBot:DroidBot Stopped`). Five of 150 sampled runs stop that way — without one in the fixture, `truncated` would be true of every input and the flag would be untested |

`tasks_slice.json` carries the task records of exactly those twelve identities. It is not a
convenience: **no baseline trace carries an end-of-run summary**, so steps total, coverage
and termination reason come from `tasks.json` or from nowhere.

Two properties of the input that the parsers are written against, and that this sample
preserves: a droidbot trace opens with thousands of androguard `DEBUG` lines before
`start sending events, policy is …` — which is why the parser skips to that line rather
than parsing from the top — and no droidbot event carries a timestamp after exploration
begins, which is why `clock` is an explicit `null` and the step index is a **synthesized**
ordinal flagged as ours (INV-CAN-19).

**Regenerating**, from the rv-android root:

```bash
.venv/bin/python modules/aperv-tool/tests/fixtures/build_baseline_sample.py
```

Read-only over the source corpus; no device (INV-APV-35).
